newsitem.title: KENYA: Power firm boosts Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Power firm boosts Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: A single lot traded on the one-hour special board for Kenya Power & Lighting boosted the Nairobi Stock Exchange marginally, bourse officials said on Friday.
The index gained 13.89 points to close at 3379.54.
Turnover was posted at 17.384 million shillings on 326,078 shares compared to 17.266 million shillings on 467,892 shares.
Kenya Power traded 30,000 shares at a reserve price of 138 from 132 on the one-hour special board.

Meanwhile foreign investors continue to boost turnover trading 5,000 shares of Tourism Promotion Services which is the trading name of Serena Lodges & Hotels SRLH at 18.50 unchanged and 34,200 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 95 and 94 from 94.

Brokers and bourse officials said the current upswing in the market this month was unlike previous years when trading would be low in May as most companies had closed their books and investors normally held out ahead of the budget in June.
"It's the influence of foreign investors. They've changed the scenario. Because of them, the market looks set to go up all the time and a lot of prices are holding steady," a senior broker said.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 115 while Standard Chartered Bank edged to 46.50 from 46.
Rea Vipingo traded at 9 from 8.95 while Kenya Airways closed at 8.60 from 8.50. Nation Printers & Publishers gained three shillings to close at 165.
Kenya Breweries was unchanged at 58 while Total Kenya closed at 66 unchanged.
